evidence.V1: Round-arch doorway with keystone reads clearly in front, three-quarter and silhouette; A15 symmetry X error 0.0, centred keystone.
evidence.V2: Big wall/opening, medium jamb blocks, voussoir ring and cornice cap, small gold keystone; clear hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Jamb blocks and voussoirs are nicely chunky, but the spandrel above is a large flat slab dominating the piece, so the overall form is only partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on jamb blocks, voussoirs, keystone and cornice catch light in springing and keystone close-ups.
evidence.V5: Clear z-fighting/brushed-noise pattern on the side faces of the jamb blocks and inside the opening (visible in end_section studio AND flat close-ups and in all colourways), plus X-shaped diagonal shading smear across the spandrel in the front view.
evidence.V6: Stone hue in 3 values (light/mid/dark block courses) plus one gold keystone accent; disciplined in brick and sandstone colourways.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, kit chamfer size, gold keystone, stone values; matches the kit apart from the artifacts.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct (Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default to keep the arch walkable, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic); T1 tiling pass (iou 1.0).

artifacts: z-fighting stipple on the side/inner faces of jamb blocks (coplanar faces of block shells and wall core)
diagonal X-shaped shading smear across the flat spandrel face
top_fixes: Remove the coplanar faces between the jamb blocks and the underlying wall core (inset the core or push the blocks proud) to kill the z-fighting
Split the spandrel into ashlar blocks or add mid-edge support loops / flat normals so the large face shades evenly
Optionally give the cornice a slight overhang profile so the top reads less like a flat slab
